🛠️ proposed fix — added to kb/known-issues.json as `ki-2026-06-02-purchase-history-unique-index-duplicate`
Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring  •  confidence: 0.88  •  alerts in group: 3  •  score: 8

Symptoms: sp_UpdateCustomerItemPurchaseHistory fails with SqlException 1505 CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IX_PA duplicate key (435,317,1); 27 distinct accounts affected over 28h; per-day 0/0/0/0/0/0/17/16 — novel issue starting 2026-06-01 07:48Z.
Trace: METHODDBCLUS1 ErrorNumber=1505; SourceContext=Runtime.Core.AppRoutine.Services.Application.Jobs.UpdatePurchaseHistoryJob; UpdatePurchaseHistoryJob.cs:238→:83.
Likely cause: recent SP migration on METHODDBCLUS1 (C# unchanged since 2026-05-13); SP populates #PriceAdjusted with duplicate rows then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IX_PA aborts.
Suggested next action: page DB/SP owner; fix candidates inside SP — add DISTINCT to INSERT, or WITH (IGNORE_DUP_KEY=ON) on IX_PA.
Source alerts (3): C063V5HTTFU/p1780390381140469, p1780390381886549, p1780390382511449.
Evidence: ES `level:Error AND "Purchase History Account - Processing Failed"`, 33 hits 2026-06-01→now; DD logs runtime-core errors window; DD APM RTC p95 clean (rules out ki-24); Kibana URL unavailable.
Investigation: docs/investigations/2026-06-02-45264ab684319413.md
Score breakdown (8): critical_path runtime-core (+3); active_users_affected=27 distinct, 21-100 bracket (+1, user_count_source: fallback — account_impact.py not_found for all 27 due to unconfigured prod3/4/5 cluster secrets); group_size 3 (+2); truly_novel (+2).

📒 known issue recurrence — ki-oauth-token-db-bloat
Occurrence #3 (3rd consecutive daily fire).
Playbook: white-check-mark indicates backup succeeded; warning is informational. Growth: 6000.81 (2026-05-31) → 6008.22 (2026-06-01) → 6016.54 (2026-06-02), ~7.8 GB/day steady, < 20 GB/day escalation threshold. No service outage. Root-cause fix path: oauth2 / ms-authentication-api — enable IdentityServer4 TokenCleanupService, add Mongo TTL on Expiration, or one-time deleteMany of expired grants. Monitoring fix: raise 5 GB advisory or per-DB exception for oauth_token.

:notebook: *known issue recurrence* -- `ki-2026-05-29-methodsession-getaccountbysubdomain-nre`
This is occurrence #6 over 5 days (occ 5->6). Layer 1 resurface: last DM was 4d ago, past the 24h suppression window.

Playbook: Centreon synthetic probe triggers `System.NullReferenceException` in `MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain()` (logged as `JWT Retrieval Failed`) on the method-platform-ui apps backend. Probe hits `/apps/api/{getsessiondata,getdashboardrightpanel/0,outlookgadget/getnavigation/0,search/recents}` without a valid Host/subdomain. The 3 CRITICAL alerts in #alert-system are Centreon's own service-checks failing (500 from the NRE).

Fix options (pick one):
  - Add a one-line null-guard in `MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain()` -> early-return on null/empty subdomain.
  - Reconfigure the Centreon probe to send a valid subdomain header.

Open Jira: none (fix_status=needs-human, fix_jira=null -- 5d unowned).

0 real-user impact (100% synthetic; WindowsPowerShell UA from 2 internal/external IPs, account id 0). Same pattern, no new evidence this cycle.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: #alert-system  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 1

*Symptoms:*
  - DD monitor 227940275 "Redis Errors is High" fired at 16:17:35Z (alert message 1780417056.843189 at 16:17:36Z).
  - Underlying metric sum:trace.redis.command.errors{env:prod}.as_count(): **79 errors at 16:12:00Z** vs threshold 10 and 24h-baseline 1 (≈79× baseline, 6.9× threshold).
  - Service breakdown of the 79 errors: nonprod/apps 70 (88%), runtime-core-api 9 (12%). No @account_name aggregation available.
  - Spike was brief — by 16:31Z down to 6+3 errors, monitor recovered to OK.

*Why this is being escalated*: third fire of monitor 227940275 today (14:08, 16:08, 16:17 UTC); prior two were grouped under ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring (co-fired with RTC). This is the first Redis-only fire today without RTC co-occurrence (RTC monitors 115456700/117279738 last triggered 14:24-14:28Z). Standing ask from prior actionable entries (15:58Z) was to formalize the RTC+Redis pattern into ki-24's playbook; this isolated fire is new evidence the Redis signal can stand alone.

*Likely cause:* The nonprod/apps service (oddly named — carries env=prod tags despite the prefix; bears the bulk of errors) is a strong candidate for monitor exclusion alongside the existing classic/syncservices-redis* and classic/methodwebservice-redis exclusions on monitor 227940275. The runtime-core-api 9-error sub-signal is small in absolute terms and consistent with chronic background Redis cache misses.

*Suggested next action:* (1) clarify what service:nonprod/apps actually is (DD service map / source code grep) — if it's truly non-prod traffic mis-tagged as env=prod, add to monitor 227940275 exclusion list; if it's a real prod component, escalate. (2) Create a formal KB entry ki-redis-errors-monitor-noisy-nonprod-apps to consolidate the recurring pattern. Holding off on KB write this cycle because confidence < 0.85 on whether to classify as false-alarm vs needs-fix until nonprod/apps provenance is known.
